Prepare weight composition data for model input

prep_wf_data.Rd

Transforms wide or long weight-frequency observations into model-ready arrays and vectors that get_weight_like() expects. Also precomputes the rebinning matrix for converting predicted length compositions to weight compositions.

Usage

prep_wf_data(
  data,
  wf_wide,
  wf_keep_fisheries = NULL,
  wf_switch = 1L,
  wf_minbin = NULL,
  wf_maxbin = NULL,
  wf_var_adjust = NULL,
  wf_cap = NULL,
  wf_addtocomp = 1e-08,
  wf_upper_edge = NULL,
  wf_tails = c("accumulate", "truncate"),
  wf_edge_tol = 1e-08 * data$wt_bin_width
)

Arguments

data

list containing at minimum: lw_a, lw_b, len_bin_start, len_bin_width, n_len, n_fishery, and the weight bin scalars wt_bin_start, wt_bin_width, n_wt.

wf_wide

A wide data frame, list of wide data frames, or long data frame. Wide frames contain fishery, year, month, ts, and numeric count columns named by bin lower edges. Long input contains the same metadata plus bin_lower, bin_upper, and count. Long observations are grouped by fishery, ts, and optionally source; calendar metadata is taken from the first row.

wf_keep_fisheries

integer vector of fishery indices to retain (NULL = keep all).

wf_switch

integer likelihood type (1=multinomial, 2=Dirichlet, 3=Dirichlet-multinomial). Default 1L.

wf_minbin

integer vector (length n_fishery) min weight bin index. Defaults to rep(1L, n_fishery).

wf_maxbin

integer vector (length n_fishery) max weight bin index. Defaults to rep(n_wt, n_fishery).

wf_var_adjust

numeric vector (length n_fishery) variance adjustment divisors. Defaults to rep(1, n_fishery).

wf_cap

positive integer (or NULL). When supplied, each effective sample size is capped: \(n_i = \min(n_i, \text{wf\_cap})\). Applied after proportions are computed so that observed compositions are unaffected. Default NULL (no cap). This is a Multifan-CL legacy feature.

wf_addtocomp

small non-negative numeric constant added to observed composition proportions after tail compression and before renormalisation. This robustifies zero bins. Default 1e-08.

wf_upper_edge

Final upper edge, or one per element of a list of wide data frames. Defaults to the largest observed bin lower edge plus data$wt_bin_width. Ignored for long input, which supplies both boundaries explicitly.

wf_tails

Prediction tail handling: "accumulate" (default) extends custom scheme matrix edges to include the converted length range; "truncate" excludes outside prediction mass. Native schemes retain the legacy finite intermediate weight range; see Details.

wf_edge_tol

Absolute tolerance for deduplicating scheme edges; defaults to 1e-8 * data$wt_bin_width.

Value

data list with the following weight composition elements appended:

wf_switch

Passed through from the argument.

wt_lower, wt_upper, wt_mid

Weight bin boundary and midpoint vectors derived from the scalar inputs.

wt_bin_edges

Weight bin boundary vector (length n_wt + 1).

wf_rebin_matrix

Precomputed rebinning matrix (n_wt x n_len) for converting predicted length compositions to weight compositions.

n_wf

Total number of WF observation rows.

wf_obs_in

Observed proportions in retained input order: a matrix with one row per observation when bin counts agree, otherwise a list of row vectors. Native input has n_wt columns.

wf_obs_flat

Flattened numeric vector of counts (for multinomial, wf_switch = 1).

wf_obs_ints

Flattened integer counts that sum to wf_n_int per observation (for Dirichlet-multinomial, wf_switch = 3).

wf_obs_prop

Flattened numeric vector of normalised proportions (for Dirichlet, wf_switch = 2).

wf_addtocomp

Stored value of the add-to-composition constant used to robustify observed composition bins.

wf_n

Numeric vector of sample sizes per observation row.

wf_n_int

Integer Dirichlet-multinomial sample sizes obtained by half-up rounding of wf_n.

wf_fishery

Integer vector of fishery index per observation row.

wf_fishery_f

Integer vector of unique fishery indices with WF data.

wf_n_f

Integer vector of observation counts per fishery.

wf_year

Integer vector of model timestep per observation row.

wf_year_fi, wf_n_fi, wf_n_int_fi, wf_row_fi

Lists split by fishery containing model timesteps, effective sample sizes, and row indices. Precomputed so opal_model() does not rebuild them on every objective evaluation.

wf_minbin, wf_maxbin

Passed through from arguments.

wf_var_adjust

Passed through from argument; numeric vector [n_fishery] of variance-adjustment divisors applied to wf_n.

Details

Input may be one wide data frame, a list of wide frames, or long data. wf_scheme_edges records observed edges, including native min/max pooling; wf_rebin_s contains observed-bin by model-length-bin prediction matrices. Length edges are converted using lw_a * L^lw_b. Native schemes preserve the legacy two-stage weight mapping and, by default, tail pooling. Even under "accumulate", native predictions outside the full native weight grid remain excluded, preserving the old numerical mapping rather than accumulating the entire converted length range. With wf_tails = "truncate", their prediction matrices select native min/max rows without accumulating excluded prediction mass. Prediction tail policy does not change observed native min/max count pooling. Native and custom weight operators remain distinct even when their displayed edges coincide, because their prediction tail handling can differ. Within each mapping type, schemes deduplicate observed edges within wf_edge_tol. Registry edges are never expanded for prediction tails. wf_scheme and wf_nbins_i follow fishery-grouped flat order; wf_row_fi indexes retained input order. Heterogeneous observations use lists where a rectangular matrix is not possible. The logical wf_native_i, in flat observation order, identifies observations originally on the full native grid before min/max pooling. Observed bins narrower than overlapping converted-length source bins trigger a warning, as do weight schemes entirely outside the source range.

Dirichlet-multinomial counts use half-up rounding of effective sample sizes and largest-remainder allocation. Observations that round to zero are skipped by the Dirichlet-multinomial likelihood.
